notes: kb/Work PB238 LANDED. Rule (cite.py OK, 14.9.4.3 rule 17, FORMAT 2): identifier-4 AND ANY IDENTIFIER inside arithmetic-expression-1 or boolean-expression-1 is a SENDING operand. ALL FOUR CHANNELS now classify, and all four are read-only. (1) identifier-4 and (2) literal-2 arrive through CallBinder.Gr8Classify, the ONE 14.9.4.4 GR8 reduction now shared by the BY CONTENT arm, the BY VALUE arm and both keyword-less arms; (3) arithmetic-expression-1 binds through host.Expr.BindExpr / BindByValueExpr; (4) BOOLEAN-EXPRESSION-1 crosses on BoundCallArg.ContentBool with ConditionBinder.Gr3Width's 8.8.2 rule-10 width, the exact counterpart of BoundInvokeArg.ContentBool that PB46 landed on the INVOKE side — it used to be REFUSED at bind with COBOL0899, so one third of the operand set was rejected on legal source. SENDING is enforced structurally: BoundStores.StoreKindVisitor.Visit(BoundCallProgram) yields a store only for `a.Mode == CobolPassMode.Reference && Hit(a.Place)`, ContentBool carries no Place at all, and CallEmitter.ArgText builds a RefCarrier only in the Reference arm. The adjudication's NEW claim ('a bare Format-2 argument is classified as receiving ... a wrong answer about an operand's direction') does NOT hold on this tree and its premise is wrong: in 14.9.4.2's Format-2 figure identifier-4 is the BY CONTENT / BY VALUE operand while the BY REFERENCE arm takes identifier-2, so a keyword-less argument that meets SR3 IS identifier-2 (GR9 a)1) and SR5 makes it receiving; only the GR9 a)2 / b) legs produce identifier-4, and those now bind Content/Value.
